title: Coefficient comparisons of the mixed-support cup product
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, integers $a,n\geq1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside a fixed $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $X_0/k_0$ be smooth of pure dimension $d\geq0$, separated of finite type and geometrically connected, and set $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $a_X:X\to s$, as in [sk-def-set]. Use the bounded constructible finite-Tor categories [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], with operations [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], coefficient cohomology complexes [sk-def-ops], and the mixed-support morphisms $\mu^\Lambda_{K,L}$ of [def-pod-mixed-support-cup-product], for $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$ and $K,L\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$.

Consider the following coefficient passages: a unital homomorphism $A_{E,n}\to A_{F,m}$ between finite coefficient rings, for finite $F/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in the chosen algebraic closure, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_F$, uniformizer $\varpi_F$, $m\geq1$, and $A_{F,m}=\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^m$, including the quotients $A_{E,n}\to A_{E,m}$ for $1\leq m\leq n$; reduction $\mathcal O_E\to A_{E,n}$; extension along $\mathcal O_E\to\mathcal O_F$ or $E\to F$ for finite $F/E$ inside $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$; rationalization $\mathcal O_E\to E$; and passage from a finite coefficient field to the common-stage $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ category. Denote such a passage by $\Lambda\to B$. For a scheme $T$, let $\Lambda_T,B_T$ denote the coefficient unit sheaves at their respective stages (completed at the integral stage). Write $S_T(M)=M\otimes^L_{\Lambda_T}B_T$ at finite coefficients, and write $S_s(C)=C\otimes^L_\Lambda B$ for the corresponding extension of coefficient complexes; these are derived changes of rings along $\Lambda_T\to B_T$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], with the derived tensor products of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. For integral reduction use [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction]; for integral extension use the completed functor of [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], and its completed coefficient-complex analogue. Rationalization uses [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], and passage to the algebraically closed category uses common finite representatives [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Denote these functors by the same symbols $S_T$ and $S_s$. Put $K_B=S_XK$, $L_B=S_XL$. There are canonical natural isomorphisms
$$
u_c:S_sR\Gamma_c(X,K)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_c(X,K_B),\qquad
u_o:S_sR\Gamma(X,L)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(X,L_B),
$$
and the analogous isomorphism $u_{c,\otimes}$ for $K\otimes^L L$, using the scalar-extension tensor comparison. Under these comparisons the following square commutes:
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
S_s\bigl(R\Gamma_c(X,K)\otimes^L_\Lambda R\Gamma(X,L)\bigr)
&\xrightarrow{S_s(\mu^\Lambda_{K,L})}& S_sR\Gamma_c(X,K\otimes^L_\Lambda L)\\
\downarrow{u_c\otimes u_o}&&\downarrow{u_{c,\otimes}}\\
R\Gamma_c(X,K_B)\otimes^L_B R\Gamma(X,L_B)
&\xrightarrow{\mu^B_{K_B,L_B}}&R\Gamma_c(X,K_B\otimes^L_B L_B).
\end{array}
$$
Here the left vertical arrow first uses the scalar-extension tensor isomorphism. The isomorphisms and squares respect identities and successive coefficient passages, and the integral cup map reduces to the finite-level cup map for every $n$. For $E$- or $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-coefficients a finite reduction is a statement about a chosen integral representative and its reductions; no reduction functor from a field to $A_{E,n}$ is asserted.
